scope: Local canonical mailbox broker and persistent TCP-loopback logical endpoints; not WAN or booted MVM capacity
endpoint_definition: Total caller plus receiver service endpoints, arranged as 1, 4 or 16 persistent TCP pairs
ordering_controls: stable owned scope with increasing sequence
dispatch: One shared broker budget, clock and synchronous local dispatcher; serial round-robin operations, pipeline one
message_mix: Alternating Call (four encrypted envelopes) and generic Cast (two encrypted envelopes)
stop_conditions: First protocol/resource error, retaining its exact stage and accepted/completed disposition
512 MiB process peak RSS or 128 observed file descriptors
profile: Explicit probe profile: 1-second retained-message extension, 1-second message TTL, native witness identity ceilings and quarter control reservation. Production defaults unchanged.
measurements: Actual framed canonical stream bytes in both directions and counter agreement
Aggregate process CPU for both endpoint roles and broker; setup separated
Admission, Reply and complete-operation p50/p95/p99 latency
Fresh-process kernel peak RSS per cell
Sampled file descriptors and post-operation state/identity maxima
Bounded time series across expiry and 60-second rate-history windows
Exact request and Call-reply payload comparisons, including zero bytes
Accepted-but-incomplete work and post-TTL cleanup without service reset
interpretation_gates: Every completed operation must recover exact bytes and length
Paced success requires no protocol errors or unverified accepted request
Saturation is classified by the actual refusal, not assumed to be Full
Stable FIFO scope counts must remain proportional to persistent streams while replay checkpoints remain retained
A fixed offered rate does not establish maximum goodput or fairness
One trial per cell establishes observations, not statistical superiority
No codec gain, durable object commit, physical energy, real WAN, native MVM fleet or final delivery claim
